messages.content: How do I view git commit logs in a single line per commit?
Run `git log --oneline` to display a compact git commit history. This command displays a compact git commit history in single lines per entry.
How do I stage all local changes for the next commit?
Run `git add .` to stage all modified and untracked files in the repository. This command stages all modified and untracked files in the repository for the next commit.
How do I create and switch to a new branch named 'dev'?
Run `git checkout -b dev` or `git switch -c dev` to create and switch to the branch. This command creates and switches to the dev branch in one step.
How do I safely discard unstaged working directory changes?
Run `git restore <filename>` to discard unstaged modifications in your working tree. This command discards unstaged modifications in your working tree for the specified filename.
How do I check current modified files in Git?
Run `git status` to view working directory and staging area status. This command displays information about both modified files and staged changes in your working directory.
How do I push a new local branch to remote repository?

Run `git push -u origin <branch_name>` to set the upstream remote tracking branch. This command pushes the local branch to the remote repository and sets up an upstream tracking reference for future updates.
How do I temporarily save uncommitted changes without committing?
Run `git stash` to temporarily save uncommitted modifications to the stash stack. This command saves your uncommitted modifications to a stash stack for later retrieval without committing them.
How do I restore the latest stashed modifications in Git?
Run `git stash pop` to apply and remove the most recent stash entry. This command applies and removes the most recent stash entry.
How do I check git commit history for a single file?
Run `git log -p filename` to view commit history and diffs for that file. This command displays commit history and diffs for that specific file.
How do I change the message of the most recent commit?
Run `git commit --amend -m 'new message'` to modify the latest commit message. This command modifies the most recent commit message in your local history.
How do I list all remote branches in Git?
Run `git branch -r` to display all remote tracking branches. This command displays all remote tracking branches in Git.
How do I delete a local branch named 'feature' safely?
Run `git branch -d feature` to safely delete the local branch. The command deletes the branch if its commits are reachable from other branches.
How do I show differences between working directory and staging area?
Run `git diff` to view unstaged modifications in your repository. This command displays differences between your working directory and staging area in your repository.
How do I merge branch 'dev' into the current branch?
Run `git merge dev` to integrate changes from the dev branch into your current branch. This command integrates changes from the dev branch into your current branch.
How do I unstage a file named 'app.py'?

Run `git restore --staged app.py` to remove the file from the staging area. This command removes 'app.py' from the staging area while keeping changes in your working directory and repository history intact.
How do I download remote updates without merging them?
Run `git fetch` to download objects and refs from the remote repository. This action downloads remote objects and references without merging them into your local repository.
How do I pull latest changes from remote and rebase?
Run `git pull --rebase` to fetch remote commits and rebase local commits on top. This command fetches remote commits and rebase local ones on top of them.
How do I view commit history as an ASCII graph?
Run `git log --graph --oneline` to display commit branching history graphically. This command displays commit branching history graphically using ASCII characters.
How do I tag the current commit as 'v1.0.0'?
Run `git tag v1.0.0` to create a lightweight tag on the current HEAD commit. This command creates a lightweight tag on the current HEAD commit.
How do I revert a specific commit safely by hash?
Run `git revert <commit_hash>` to create a new commit that undoes specified changes. This command creates a new commit that undoes specified changes.
How do I clone a git repository recursively with submodules?
Run `git clone --recursive <url>` to clone the repository along with all submodules. This command clones the repository along with all submodules.
How do I inspect who last modified each line of a file?
Run `git blame <filename>` to view author and revision information for each line. This command displays author and revision information for each line of the specified filename.
How do I apply a specific commit from another branch?
Run `git cherry-pick <commit_hash>` to apply the changes from that commit. This command applies the changes from that specific commit to your current branch.
How do I check which branch contains a specific commit?
Run `git branch --contains <commit_hash>` to list branches including that commit. This command lists all branches that include the specified commit in their history.
How do I list saved stash entries in Git?
Run `git stash list` to inspect all saved stash stack entries. This command displays all saved stash stack entries for inspection.
How do I rename the current Git branch to 'main'?
Run `git branch -M main` to rename your current active branch to main. This command renames your current active branch to main while keeping you on that renamed branch.
How do I perform a dry-run check of untracked files before cleaning?
Run `git clean -nd` to preview untracked files that would be removed. This command previews untracked files that would be removed without actually deleting them.
How do I check configured remote URLs in Git?
Run `git remote -v` to list all configured remote repository names and URLs. This command displays all configured remote repository names and their associated URLs for your current Git installation.
How do I ignore file mode permission changes in Git?
Run `git config core.fileMode false` to stop tracking file executable bit changes. This setting stops Git from tracking changes to executable bits in files.
How do I create a patch file from the latest commit?
Run `git format-patch -1 HEAD` to generate a patch file from the last commit. This command generates a patch file representing the last commit.
How do I soft-reset the HEAD to the previous commit while keeping changes staged?
Run `git reset --soft HEAD~1` to move HEAD back while preserving changes. This command moves HEAD to the previous commit while keeping changes staged for future commits.
How do I view the commit log for the last 5 commits?
Run `git log -n 5 --oneline` to view the last 5 commits in short format. This command displays the specified number of recent commits using short format for brevity and clarity in the output log.
How do I compare commits between main and dev branches?

Run `git diff main..dev` to inspect differences between main and dev branches. This command inspects differences between main and dev branches by running git diff main..dev to inspect differences between main and dev branches.
How do I show the contents of a specific commit?
Run `git show <commit_hash>` to display details and diff of a commit. This command displays details and diff of the specified commit.
How do I check out a specific tag in Git?
Run `git checkout v1.0.0` to inspect the code at tag v1.0.0. This command allows you to inspect the code at tag v1.0.0 as stated in the trusted answer.
How do I list all local and remote branches in Git?
Run `git branch -a` to display both local and remote tracking branches. This command displays both local and remote tracking branches in Git.
How do I abort an in-progress merge conflict?
Run `git merge --abort` to cancel the merge and restore pre-merge state. This command cancels the merge and restores the pre-merge state.
How do I abort an in-progress rebase?
Run `git rebase --abort` to stop the rebase and return to original branch state. This command stops the rebase and returns to the original branch state.
How do I set your Git user name globally?
Run `git config --global user.name 'Your Name'` to configure global commit author. This command sets your Git user name globally to configure global commit author.
How do I set your Git user email globally?
Run `git config --global user.email 'email@example.com'` to configure commit email. This command sets your Git user email globally to configure commit email.
How do I search recursively for text 'ERROR' in log files?
Run `grep -rn 'ERROR' /var/log/` to search recursively with line numbers. This command searches recursively through files in /var/log/ for text matching ERROR while displaying line numbers.
How do I find all Python files in current directory recursively?
Run `find . -name '*.py'` to locate all Python source files in subdirectories. This command locates all Python source files in subdirectories using find with a wildcard pattern for .py extensions.
How do I make a shell script executable in Linux?
Run `chmod +x script.sh` to grant execution permissions to the script file. This command grants execution permissions to the script file.
How do I view real-time system process activity in Linux?
Run `top` or `htop` to display active system processes and resource usage. This allows you to view real-time system process activity in Linux.
How do I check available memory in human-readable units?
Run `free -h` to display total, used, and available RAM and swap space. This command displays total, used, and available RAM and swap space in human-readable units.
How do I check disk space usage of mounted filesystems?
Run `df -h` to view disk capacity and usage for all mounted filesystems. This command displays disk capacity and usage for all mounted filesystems.
How do I measure directory size in human-readable format?
Run `du -sh /path/to/dir` to calculate total size of a directory. This command calculates total size of a directory and displays result in human-readable format.
How do I continuously follow new lines added to a log file?
Run `tail -f app.log` to stream new log output in real time. This command streams new log output in real time.
How do I send a graceful termination signal to process ID 1234?
Run `kill -15 1234` to send a standard SIGTERM signal to process ID 1234. This command sends SIGTERM to process ID 1234 as described in the trusted answer.
How do I print the active absolute working directory path?
Run `pwd` to print the full path of your current working directory. This command prints the full path of your current working directory.
How do I list all files including hidden files with details?
Run `ls -la` to list all files, permissions, owners, and hidden dotfiles. This command displays details for all files including hidden dotfiles in addition to regular items.
How do I compress a folder named 'src' into a tar.gz archive?
Run `tar -czvf src.tar.gz src/` to create a compressed gzipped tar archive. This command creates a compressed tar archive named src.tar.gz containing the contents of the src directory.
How do I extract a tar.gz archive named 'data.tar.gz'?
Run `tar -xzvf data.tar.gz` to extract all contents from the tar archive. This command extracts all contents from the tar archive as specified in the trusted answer.
How do I check HTTP response headers for a URL using curl?
Run `curl -I https://example.com` to fetch and display HTTP response headers. This command fetches and displays HTTP response headers for the specified URL.
How do I check listening network ports on Linux?
Run `ss -tulpn` to list all active listening TCP and UDP sockets. This command lists all active listening TCP and UDP sockets on Linux systems.
How do I check environment variables set in current shell?
Run `env` or `printenv` to print all active shell environment variables. This command displays all active shell environment variables currently in effect.
How do I create a symbolic link named 'link' to 'target'?
Run `ln -s target link` to create a symbolic link pointing to the target file. This command creates a symbolic link named 'link' that points to 'target'.
How do I check Linux kernel version and architecture?
Run `uname -a` to print system architecture, hostname, and kernel version. This command prints system architecture, hostname, and kernel version.
How do I measure command execution runtime in Bash?
Prefix your command with `time`, such as `time python script.py`. This prefixes your command with time to measure its execution runtime in Bash.
How do I redirect stdout and stderr to the same log file?
Run `command > output.log 2>&1` to redirect both output streams into one file. This redirects both output streams into one file as stated in the trusted answer.
How do I locate the binary path of an installed command?
Run `which python3` to display the executable path for the specified command. This command displays the executable path for the specified command.
How do I count total lines in a CSV text file?
Run `wc -l dataset.csv` to count the total number of lines in the file. This command counts every line in the specified CSV text file to provide its total number of lines.
How do I sort lines in a file and remove duplicates?
Run `sort file.txt | uniq` to sort lines and output unique entries. This command sorts lines and outputs unique entries by removing duplicates.
How do I filter out lines containing the string 'DEBUG'?
Run `grep -v 'DEBUG' log.txt` to invert match and exclude matching lines. This command inverts the match to exclude lines containing 'DEBUG' from log.txt output.
How do I send a POST HTTP request with JSON payload using curl?

Run `curl -X POST https://api.example.com/data -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"a":1}'`. This command sends data to an API endpoint using JSON formatting as specified in the request headers and payload.
How do I recursively change directory ownership to user 'ubuntu'?
Run `sudo chown -R ubuntu:ubuntu /path/to/dir` to recursively change owner. This command recursively changes directory ownership to user ubuntu and group ubuntu for all files in the specified path.
How do I check Linux system uptime and load average?
Run `uptime` to view system running time, active users, and load averages. The command displays system running time and load averages along with active users.
How do I safely remove a file with confirmation prompt?
Run `rm -i filename` to remove the file with an interactive confirmation prompt. This command displays an interactive confirmation prompt before removing the specified filename.
How do I view differences between two text files line by line?
Run `diff file1.txt file2.txt` to compare line differences between two files. This command displays line differences between two files when executed in your terminal environment.
How do I monitor NVIDIA GPU memory and utilization?
Run `nvidia-smi` to inspect NVIDIA GPU memory consumption and GPU load. This command allows you to inspect NVIDIA GPU memory consumption and GPU load.
How do I create a directory hierarchy recursively in Linux?
Run `mkdir -p /path/to/nested/dir` to create parent directories as needed. This command creates parent directories as needed to establish the specified path structure recursively.
How do I search for text ignoring case in grep?
Run `grep -i 'pattern' file.txt` to perform a case-insensitive search. This command performs a case-insensitive search using the -i flag with grep and file.txt as specified in the trusted answer.
How do I view first 20 lines of a text file?
Run `head -n 20 file.txt` to display the first 20 lines of the file. This command displays the first 20 lines of the specified text file using the head utility with the -n flag set to twenty.
How do I view last 20 lines of a text file?
Run `tail -n 20 file.txt` to display the last 20 lines of the file. This command displays the last 20 lines of the specified text file using the tail utility with an n flag argument.
How do I change file permissions to read-only for all?
Run `chmod 444 file.txt` to set read-only permissions for owner, group, and others. This command sets read-only permissions for owner, group, and others on the specified file.
How do I display line numbers when viewing a file with cat?
Run `cat -n file.txt` to print file contents with line numbers. This command prints line numbers alongside the file contents when viewing with cat.
How do I search for active processes owned by user 'ubuntu'?
Run `ps -u ubuntu` to list all active processes belonging to user ubuntu. This command lists all active processes belonging to user ubuntu.
How do I check memory usage in megabytes in Linux?
Run `free -m` to view total and available memory in megabytes. This command displays total and available memory in megabytes.
How do I print environment variable PATH in Bash?
Run `echo $PATH` to print current executable search path entries. This command displays the current executable search path entries in your system environment.
How do I alias a shell command in Bash?
Add `alias ll='ls -la'` to your `~/.bashrc` file to create a command alias. This adds an alias to your ~/.bashrc file to create a command alias.
How do I read and parse a JSON file in Python?
Use `json.load()` within a `with open('data.json') as f:` context block. This method reads and parses JSON data directly into Python objects using the specified context manager for file handling.
How do I write a Python dictionary to a formatted JSON file?
Use `json.dump(data, f, indent=2)` to serialize dictionary data to JSON. This function writes the dictionary data to the specified JSON format within the provided file object.
How do I send an HTTP GET request in Python using requests?
Use `requests.get('https://example.com')` to fetch data from an HTTP endpoint. This method fetches data from an HTTP endpoint using requests.get().
How do I create a Python virtual environment in directory '.venv'?
Run `python3 -m venv .venv` to initialize a new Python virtual environment. This command initializes a new Python virtual environment in the specified directory named .venv.
How do I install dependencies listed in requirements.txt?
Run `pip install -r requirements.txt` to install all listed packages. This command installs all packages listed in requirements.txt using pip.
How do I handle runtime exceptions gracefully in Python?

Wrap execution inside a `try:` block and catch errors using `except Exception as e:`. This approach allows you to handle runtime exceptions gracefully by catching errors within the specified block structure.
How do I parse command line flags using argparse in Python?

Initialize `argparse.ArgumentParser()`, add args with `add_argument()`, and call `parse_args()`. This process initializes an argument parser and parses command line arguments to retrieve their values for program execution.
How do I measure precise execution time in Python?
Import `time` and compute elapsed time using `time.perf_counter()`. This method computes elapsed time using `time.perf_counter()`.
How do I access operating system environment variables in Python?
Import `os` and retrieve variables using `os.getenv('VAR_NAME', 'default')`. This method retrieves variables by name and returns a default value if none is found for that key.
How do I define a data class in Python?

Decorate your class definition with `@dataclass` from the `dataclasses` module. The decorator is used to define a data class in Python by decorating your class definition with @dataclass from the dataclasses module.
How do I check if a key exists in a Python dictionary?
Use the `in` operator, such as `if 'key' in my_dict:`. This check evaluates to true if the key is present in the dictionary and false otherwise.
How do I merge two dictionaries in Python 3.9+?
Use the union operator, such as `merged_dict = dict1 | dict2`. This operator merges two dictionaries into one using Python 3.9+.
How do I convert a list of strings into a single comma-separated string?
Use the string join method, such as `', '.join(string_list)`. This method combines each item in the list with commas to produce one continuous string result.
How do I remove leading and trailing whitespace from a Python string?
Call `.strip()` on the string instance, such as `cleaned_text = raw_text.strip()`. This method removes leading and trailing whitespace from the string instance.
How do I sort a list of dictionaries by a specific key in Python?

Use `sorted(data, key=lambda x: x['key_name'])` or `data.sort(key=...)`. This sorts the list based on values associated with 'key_name' using either sorted() for immutable lists or sort() to modify in place.
How do I create a shallow copy of a list in Python?

Use `.copy()` method or slice syntax, such as `new_list = old_list.copy()`. This creates a shallow copy of the list in Python using either the .copy() method or slice syntax like `new_list = old_list.copy()`.
How do I flatten a 2D list into a 1D list in Python?
Use a list comprehension, such as `[item for sublist in matrix for item in sublist]`. This method iterates through each sublist and collects every item into a single list structure.
How do I read lines of a text file into a list in Python?
Use `with open('file.txt') as f: lines = f.read().splitlines()`. This method reads all lines into a list by splitting on line breaks without including newline characters in each item.
How do I check the length of a list or string in Python?
Pass the object to the built-in function `len()`, such as `len(my_list)`. The function returns an integer representing the count of items in the list or characters in the string.
How do I convert a string representation of an integer to an int?
Pass the string to `int()`, such as `num = int('123')`. Passing the string to int() converts its text representation into an integer value for further processing.
How do I iterate over index and element simultaneously in Python?
Use `enumerate()`, such as `for idx, item in enumerate(my_list):`. This function returns both the index and element for each item in an iterable during iteration.
How do I define an asynchronous function in Python?
Prefix the function declaration with `async def my_func():`. This syntax allows Python to handle asynchronous operations using the async and await keywords within coroutines.
How do I run an async function in Python 3.7+?
Import `asyncio` and execute `asyncio.run(my_async_function())`. This method executes the async function within an event loop context provided by asyncio.
How do I get unique elements from a list while preserving order in Python?
Use `list(dict.fromkeys(my_list))` to deduplicate elements while retaining order. This method creates unique elements while preserving their original order in Python lists.
How do I check if all elements in a list satisfy a condition in Python?
Use the built-in `all()` function with a generator expression. The `all()` function returns True if every element in the iterable satisfies the provided condition when evaluated as truthy values.
How do I check if at least one element satisfies a condition in Python?
Use the built-in `any()` function with a generator expression. The function returns True if at least one element satisfies the condition and False otherwise when no elements do.
How do I filter elements in a list in Python?
Use list comprehension, such as `filtered = [x for x in data if x > 0]`. This method creates a new list containing elements that satisfy the specified condition within the original data structure.
How do I set a default value when getting a missing dictionary key?
Use `.get('key', default_value)` method on the dictionary instance. This method returns the specified default value if the key is missing from the dictionary.
How do I execute a shell command from Python and get output?
Import `subprocess` and run `subprocess.run(['ls', '-l'], capture_output=True, text=True)`. This executes the command and retrieves its output as text.
How do I load environment variables from a .env file in Python?
Import `dotenv` and execute `dotenv.load_dotenv()` at startup. This loads environment variables defined in the .env file at startup.
How do I convert a string to lowercase in Python?
Call `.lower()` on the string, such as `text.lower()`. This method converts all characters in the string to lowercase letters using Python's built-in function.
How do I convert a string to uppercase in Python?
Call `.upper()` on the string, such as `text.upper()`. This method converts all characters in the string to uppercase letters.
How do I check if a string starts with a prefix in Python?
Call `.startswith('prefix')` on the string instance. This method returns True if the string begins with the specified prefix and False otherwise.
How do I check if a string ends with a suffix in Python?
Call `.endswith('suffix')` on the string instance. This method returns True if the string ends with the specified suffix and False otherwise.
How do I replace substrings in a Python string?
Call `.replace('old', 'new')` on the target string instance. This method returns a modified string with occurrences of old replaced by new.
How do I convert a list of integers to a set in Python?
Pass the list to `set()`, such as `my_set = set(my_list)`. This converts each integer in my_list into unique elements within my_set by removing any duplicates automatically.
How do I write a binary file in Python?
Open the file with `'wb'` mode, such as `with open('file.bin', 'wb') as f: f.write(data)`. This method writes data to a binary file using Python's built-in open function with write-binary mode.
How do I read a binary file in Python?
Open the file with `'rb'` mode, such as `with open('file.bin', 'rb') as f: data = f.read()`. This reads all content into memory as bytes using binary mode to preserve data integrity during retrieval.
How do I import a module dynamically in Python?
Import `importlib` and execute `importlib.import_module('module_name')`. This method allows you to import modules by their string name at runtime using the specified function call.
How do I format float numbers to 2 decimal places in Python?
Use f-string formatting, such as `f'{value:.2f}'`. This method formats float values to display exactly two decimal places using f-string syntax in Python code.
How do I list running Docker containers?
Run `docker ps` to display all currently active Docker containers. This command displays all currently active Docker containers.
How do I list all Docker containers including stopped ones?
Run `docker ps -a` to list all active and exited Docker containers. This command lists all active and exited Docker containers.
How do I build a Docker image from a Dockerfile in current folder?
Run `docker build -t myapp:latest .` to compile the image. This command compiles the image using the Dockerfile in the current directory and tags it as myapp:latest.
How do I stop a running Docker container named 'web'?
Run `docker stop web` to send a graceful shutdown signal to the container. This command stops the container named web by sending a graceful shutdown signal to it.
How do I view logs from a Docker container named 'api'?
Run `docker logs -f api` to stream live output logs from the container. This command streams live output logs from the container named api using docker logs -f api.
How do I execute an interactive bash shell inside a running container?
Run `docker exec -it <container_id> /bin/bash` to enter the container. This command allows you to start an interactive bash shell session within the specified running container instance.
How do I remove an unused Docker image?
Run `docker rmi <image_id>` or `docker image prune` to delete unused images. This removes unused images using either the specific image ID or by pruning all dangling ones.
How do I start services defined in a docker-compose.yml file?
Run `docker-compose up -d` to launch all defined services in background mode. This command launches all defined services in background mode as specified by the docker-compose.yml file.
How do I stop services defined in docker-compose.yml?
Run `docker-compose down` to stop and remove containers, networks, and volumes. This command stops and removes containers, networks, and volumes as stated in the original answer.
How do I inspect details of a Docker container?
Run `docker inspect <container_id>` to view full JSON metadata of the container. This command displays full JSON metadata of the container.
How do I select all columns from a table named 'users' in SQL?
Execute `SELECT * FROM users;` in your SQL database client. This command retrieves every column and row present in the users table within your SQL database client.
How do I filter rows where age is greater than 18 in SQL?
Execute `SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > 18;` in SQL. This query retrieves all records where the age column value exceeds 18 in the users table using standard SQL syntax.
How do I count total records in a table named 'orders' in SQL?
Execute `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders;` to get total row count. This query retrieves the total number of rows present in the orders table.
How do I update a user's email safely in SQL?
Execute `UPDATE users SET email = 'new@example.com' WHERE id = 1;`. This statement updates the email for user with id 1 to the specified address in the users table.
How do I query inactive users in SQL?
Execute `SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = 'inactive';` in your SQL client. This query retrieves all records where the status field is set to inactive in the users table.
How do I sort SQL query results by creation date descending?
Append `ORDER BY created_at DESC` to your SQL SELECT query. This clause arranges the returned rows so that records with later creation dates appear first in the result set.
How do I limit SQL query results to 10 rows?
Append `LIMIT 10` to your SQL query statement. This clause restricts the output to exactly 10 rows in your query results.
How do I join two tables 'orders' and 'users' on user_id in SQL?
Use `SELECT * FROM orders JOIN users ON orders.user_id = users.id;`. This query joins two tables on user_id to retrieve data from both orders and users in one result set.
How do I create a primary key index on table 'products' in SQL?
Use `ALTER TABLE products ADD PRIMARY KEY (id);`. This command adds a primary key index to table 'products' on column id.
How do I insert a new row into table 'users' in SQL?
Execute `INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('Alice', 'alice@example.com');`. This command adds one row containing Alice and alice@example.com to the users table.
How do I send a JSON POST request in JavaScript fetch API?
Call `fetch(url, {method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: data})`. This request sends data to the specified URL using the POST method with JSON formatting in the body.
How do I parse a JSON string into an object in JavaScript?
Use `JSON.parse(json_string)` to deserialize JSON into a JavaScript object. This method converts the provided JSON string into an actual JavaScript object structure.
How do I convert a JavaScript object into a JSON string?
Use `JSON.stringify(object)` to serialize an object into a JSON string. This method converts an object into a JSON string format for storage or transmission purposes.
How do I declare an async function in JavaScript?
Use syntax `async function fetchData() { const res = await fetch(url); }`. This syntax allows you to define an async function that can pause execution using await with fetch.
How do I handle rejected promises in JavaScript async/await?
Wrap your await call in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. This structure allows you to catch errors that occur when an await call rejects its promise.
How do I add an element to the end of an array in JavaScript?
Call `.push(element)` on the array instance, such as `arr.push('item')`. This method appends the specified element to the end of the array instance.
How do I remove the last element of an array in JavaScript?
Call `.pop()` on the array instance, such as `const last = arr.pop()`. The method removes and returns that final item from the array instance.
How do I iterate over an array in JavaScript with element and index?
Use `array.forEach((item, index) => { ... })`. This method allows you to access both the current item and its index within each iteration of the array.
How do I map array elements to a new array in JavaScript?
Use `array.map(x => x * 2)` to transform each element. The map function creates a new array by applying the provided callback to each element of the original array.
How do I filter array elements matching a condition in JavaScript?
Use `array.filter(x => x > 10)` to extract matching items. This method extracts items that satisfy the specified condition into a new array.
How do I check container port mappings in Docker?
Run `docker port <container_id>` to view published container ports. This command displays which host ports are mapped to specific container ports for network access.
How do I restart a running Docker container?
Run `docker restart <container_id>` to restart the container. This command restarts the container without changing its name or ID.
How do I view Docker resource stats in real time?
Run `docker stats` to monitor CPU, memory, and network usage per container. This command allows you to monitor CPU, memory, and network usage per container in real time.
How do I pause execution of a running Docker container?
Run `docker pause <container_id>` to suspend container execution. This command suspends container execution without stopping it completely.
How do I unpause a suspended Docker container?
Run `docker unpause <container_id>` to resume execution of a paused container. This command resumes execution of the paused container.
How do I create a new network in Docker?
Run `docker network create my_network` to create an isolated bridge network. This command creates an isolated bridge network named my_network for Docker containers to communicate with each other.
How do I list all Docker networks?
Run `docker network ls` to inspect all configured Docker networks. This command lists all configured Docker networks for inspection.
How do I create a named Docker volume?
Run `docker volume create my_volume` to allocate a persistent storage volume. This command allocates persistent storage for your data.
How do I list all named Docker volumes?
Run `docker volume ls` to list existing persistent Docker volumes. This command lists all named Docker volumes that exist in your current environment.
How do I select unique values of a column in SQL?
Execute `SELECT DISTINCT column_name FROM table_name;` in SQL. This query returns each unique value found in that specific column within the specified table.
How do I connect to a remote server using SSH on port 2222?
Run `ssh -p 2222 user@hostname` to connect via SSH on a custom port. This command connects via SSH on port 2222 to the specified user and hostname.
How do I copy a local file to a remote server using SCP?
Run `scp -P 2222 file.txt user@hostname:/remote/path/`. This command copies the specified local file to the designated remote path on the server using port 2222.
How do I generate a 4096-bit RSA SSH key pair?
Run `ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C 'email@example.com'`. This command generates an RSA key pair with 4096 bits of length and includes your email address as a comment in the output file.
How do I copy my public SSH key to a remote server for passwordless login?
Run `ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub user@hostname`. This command copies your public key to enable passwordless login for that user and hostname.
How do I test DNS resolution for a domain name using dig?
Run `dig example.com +short` to perform a DNS lookup. This command performs a DNS lookup for example.com and displays the result in short format.
How do I trace network packet routing hops to a target server?
Run `traceroute example.com` or `mtr example.com` to trace network paths. This traces network packet routing hops to a target server.
How do I check latency and packet loss to a host?
Run `ping -c 4 example.com` to send 4 ICMP echo requests. This command sends four ICMP echo requests to check latency and packet loss to the host.
How do I check systemd service status for nginx?
Run `systemctl status nginx` to inspect systemd unit status. This command inspects systemd unit status for nginx.
How do I restart a systemd service named 'postgresql'?
Run `sudo systemctl restart postgresql` to restart the service. This command restarts the postgresql service using systemd's built-in management tools.
How do I enable a systemd service to start automatically on boot?
Run `sudo systemctl enable nginx` to enable auto-start at boot time. This command configures systemd to start nginx automatically when the system boots up.
How do I view systemd journal logs for unit 'docker'?
Run `journalctl -u docker -n 50 --no-pager` to view recent unit logs. This command displays recent logs for the specified unit without using the pager interface.
How do I check current firewall status in Ubuntu using ufw?
Run `sudo ufw status verbose` to view active firewall rules. This command displays active firewall rules in verbose mode to check current status.
How do I allow incoming port 443 in ufw firewall?
Run `sudo ufw allow 443/tcp` to permit incoming HTTPS traffic. This command permits incoming HTTPS traffic on port 443 through ufw.
How do I generate an MD5 checksum of a file in Linux?
Run `md5sum filename` to compute the MD5 hash digest. This command computes the MD5 hash digest for the specified filename.
How do I generate a SHA256 checksum of a file?
Run `sha256sum filename` to compute the SHA256 hash digest. This command computes the SHA256 hash digest for filename as specified in the trusted answer.
How do I check SSL certificate expiration date for a domain?
Run `openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates`. This command displays the certificate's start and end dates to verify its expiration status.
How do I create a self-signed SSL certificate using OpenSSL?

Run `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -nodes`. This command generates both the key and certificate files in one step using RSA encryption with 2048-bit strength for three hundred sixty-five days.
How do I monitor disk I/O activity per process in Linux?
Run `sudo iotop` to monitor real-time disk read/write bandwidth by process. This command monitors real-time disk read/write bandwidth by process.
How do I monitor network throughput per interface in Linux?
Run `iftop` or `nload` to monitor real-time network traffic per interface. This allows you to monitor real-time network traffic per interface using iftop or nload.
How do I find which process is using port 8080?
Run `lsof -i :8080` or `fuser 8080/tcp` to identify the owning process. This identifies which process is using port 8080 by listing its owner.
How do I send a term signal to the process using port 8080?
Run `fuser -k -15 8080/tcp` to send a graceful term signal to the process. This command sends a graceful term signal to terminate the process listening on port 8080/tcp.
How do I check system kernel messages using dmesg?

Run `dmesg -T | tail -n 50` to print recent kernel ring buffer messages. This command prints recent kernel ring buffer messages to display them in chronological order with timestamps and limited lines.
How do I reload Nginx configuration without dropping connections?
Run `sudo systemctl reload nginx` or `nginx -s reload`. This reloads Nginx to apply changes without dropping connections.
How do I test Nginx configuration syntax for errors?
Run `sudo nginx -t` to verify configuration syntax before reloading. This command verifies configuration syntax before reloading.
How do I list active crontab scheduled jobs for current user?
Run `crontab -l` to view all configured cron jobs for your user. This command lists all configured cron jobs for your user.
How do I edit active crontab scheduled jobs?
Run `crontab -e` to open the cron schedule configuration in your editor. This command opens your current cron schedule for editing in an editor of your choice.
How do I schedule a script to run every day at midnight in cron?
Add line `0 0 * * * /path/to/script.sh` to your crontab file. This line schedules your script to execute daily at midnight by adding it to your crontab file.
How do I schedule a script to run every 5 minutes in cron?
Add line `*/5 * * * * /path/to/script.sh` to your crontab file. This line tells cron to execute the specified script every five minutes as defined by the schedule pattern.
How do I set environment variable PATH permanently in Bash?
Add `export PATH="/new/path:$PATH"` to your `~/.bashrc` file. This adds the export command to your bashrc so that PATH is updated every time you start a new terminal session.
How do I reload shell configuration after modifying .bashrc?
Run `source ~/.bashrc` to apply the updated environment configuration. This command applies the updated environment configuration to your current session.
How do I create a zip archive of a directory in Linux?
Run `zip -r archive.zip folder_name/` to create a zip file. This command creates a zip archive containing all files and subdirectories within folder_name with an r flag for recursive inclusion.
How do I unzip a zip file named 'archive.zip'?
Run `unzip archive.zip` to extract files from the zip archive. This command extracts files from the zip archive as stated in the original answer.
How do I download a web page source HTML using wget?
Run `wget -O page.html https://example.com` to download page source. This command saves the downloaded HTML content into a file named page.html on your local system.
How do I sync files from local directory to remote server using rsync?
Run `rsync -avz /local/dir/ user@remote:/remote/dir/`. This command copies files from your local directory to the specified remote path on the server.
How do I perform a dry run of an rsync sync command?
Run `rsync -avz --dry-run /local/dir/ user@remote:/remote/dir/`. This command simulates the transfer process without actually moving any files to verify syntax and paths first.
How do I check open file descriptor limits in Linux?
Run `ulimit -n` to view the maximum allowed open file descriptors per process. This command displays the maximum allowed open file descriptors per process.
How do I temporarily increase open file descriptor limit to 65536?
Run `ulimit -n 65536` in your current shell session. This command temporarily increases the open file descriptor limit to 65536 in your current shell session.
How do I view CPU model and core information in Linux?
Run `lscpu` or `cat /proc/cpuinfo` to inspect CPU hardware details. This allows you to view CPU model and core information in Linux as stated in the trusted answer.
How do I check current system hostname in Linux?
Run `hostname` or `hostnamectl` to display the machine hostname. This command displays the machine hostname to identify the current system name for display purposes.
How do I change machine hostname permanently in Ubuntu?
Run `sudo hostnamectl set-hostname new-hostname` to update machine name. This command updates the machine name permanently in Ubuntu.
